newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia's Great River seeks Asian expansion.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Great River seeks Asian expansion.

text.p: Jakarta-listed clothing company PT Great River International is expanding across Asia Pacific in a bid to be the region's largest distributor, president director Sunjoto Tanudjaja said on Tuesday.

"Our goal is to grow the company by continuing to expand and stengthen our distribution channels in Indonesia and the region. I'd like to see PT Great River become the largest apparel distributor in the Asia Pacific," Tanudjaja said at a corporate presentation.
The company, which makes, distributes and sells products in Indonesia and Asia, would be looking for more partners to foster alliances for expansion, he said.
He did not dismiss the possibility of future mergers or acquisitions but said the group's plans were cautious.
Tanudjaja told Reuters after the conference that the company had made a business proposal to a Singapore-listed company with some retail links, but declined to give further details.

Tanudjaja, who co-founded the company with his father, Sukanta Tanudjaja, in 1976, said the company had identified the Asia-Pacific as the most promising market outside Indonesia due to its strong economic growth and high disposable incomes.

Great River is targetting net profit to rise to a minimum of 26 billion rupiah ($11 million) for its fiscal year ending December 31 1996, up from 13.3 billion rupiah in 1995. Net sales are also expected to see a significant rise to 254 billion rupiah this year compared to 182.3 billion last year.
Tanudjaja said while manufacturing remained the company's core business, its focus was on retail and distribution, which account for 70 percent of the company's business.
He added the company was moving aggressively into direct selling to wholesalers and retail shops and expanding distribution in Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore.
Malaysia and Singapore contribute about six percent of the company's sales, and Tanudjaja said he saw this growing to 10-14 percent from next year.
Great River plans to add another 15-20 new distribution licences and agencies in 1998 to its current list of 36 licences and 16 agencies.
The company holds 52 well-known international brands in ladieswear, menwear, casual and accessories.
Tanudjaja said he was optimistic about the clothing industry, notably after the full formation of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) Free Trade Area (AFTA).
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam .
"We will have a market that will grow to 450 million people, which is more than double what we have in Indonesia, and with a higher purchasing power." ($1 = 2,345 rupiah)
